tvs.text-bl-seo-2:
Stages of the micropigmentation procedure

Whatever the area and the semi-permanent makeup technique, the procedure always follows certain stages.

Initial consultation

The artist reviews your medical history to make sure there are no contraindications to the procedure and to check your general health at the time of the session. Then, together with you, the artist selects the pigment shade based on your color type and the rules of color theory. Please note: we don't work with black pigments. If you want very dark brows, the artist will choose a dark shade of brown. However, this option is rarely chosen, as very dark brows look unnatural. Most often a lighter shade is chosen to create a natural effect. For tattooing the eyes, black is used. The liner can be any shade, but black is universal and considered the best option. For lip tattooing, pastel and nude colors are used: pink, coral. The color can range in intensity from pale to vivid, depending on your preferences.

Creating the sketch

The artist never starts the procedure without this stage. Why is it necessary? So that you can see the shape of the future tattoo: the width of the brows or the eyeliner style. For lip tattooing, the outline is determined by the natural shape of the lips. While applying the pigment, the artist may go slightly beyond the natural lip line to add volume or hide asymmetry. However, this is done sensibly so that the effect stays natural. The sketch also lets the artist see the boundaries and not go beyond them.

Performing the micropigmentation

No anesthetic is applied before the procedure starts. This is because the procedure itself isn't very painful, so there's no need for an anesthetic at the first stage. It is used later, after several passes of the device over the area, when the skin is already traumatized. A numbing cream is applied to the area and left to take effect, relieving pain, redness and swelling. Then the artist continues the procedure. The anesthetic may be applied several times, depending on how your skin reacts.

Follow-up consultation. At the end of the procedure, the artist cleanses the skin with chlorhexidine, gives you aftercare advice, hands you a brochure with detailed instructions and books your touch-up appointment. With your consent, the artist will take a photo of the finished work to add to the portfolio.

Is a touch-up of semi-permanent makeup necessary?

If you want the final result of your semi-permanent makeup, which you'll wear for at least a year, to be accurate and beautiful, then a touch-up is a must. It saturates the area with pigment, gives the semi-permanent makeup its finishing touch and perfects any areas where minor imperfections appeared during healing. During the touch-up, the shape can be slightly adjusted if you wish. For example, you can make the brows, the contour or the lips bigger or fuller.

Contraindications to micropigmentation

The artist will refuse to perform the procedure if you have a medical condition that is a contraindication. These include insulin-dependent diabetes, epilepsy, viral diseases and cancer, immunodeficiency, skin inflammation in the tattoo area, high blood pressure and fever.
Semi-permanent makeup can be done during your period.

Tattoo aftercare

Aftercare may vary depending on your skin type and your body's individual reaction to the pigment and to the procedure in general. The artist will observe how your body reacts during the session and tell you which healing, regenerating and moisturizing skin products are recommended for you – or may tell you that you don't need any. If products have been recommended, it's important to follow the recommendations and not to self-treat. Otherwise, aftercare follows the standard guidelines:

  • don't steam the skin. Avoid long showers, hot baths, saunas, jacuzzis and swimming pools;
  • wash the tattooed area with lukewarm water and a gentle cleanser, such as liquid baby soap;
  • don't tan while your skin is recovering. Avoid tanning beds. When you go outdoors, keep the treated areas out of direct sunlight or apply a high-SPF sunscreen, at least SPF 40;
  • avoid any physical impact on the freshly tattooed area: no scratching, no picking off flaking skin and no cosmetic procedures that traumatize the skin (peels, exfoliation).

At the end of the session, the artist will explain aftercare in detail and give recommendations for your particular case. Following them is important to preserve the result of your makeup.

How long micropigmentation lasts

How long the effect lasts depends on the area. At our micropigmentation studio, the artist gives the following timeframes: brows and lips – up to 2 years, eyelids – up to 3 years. It also depends on your skin type, lifestyle and individual characteristics. On dry skin the effect lasts longer, on oily skin – shorter. Likewise, in younger people the effect fades sooner, while in older people it lasts longer.

migx_questions.questions-title: Are cosmetic tattooing and micropigmentation the same procedure?
migx_questions.questions-text: Basically, yes – if by cosmetic tattooing we mean the modern procedure. Broadly speaking, the two terms are synonyms. In the early '90s, when cosmetic tattooing first appeared, it was very different from modern semi-permanent makeup. Back then, outdated machines and different shades were used, and the pigment was injected deep into the skin, so a tattoo lasted for years, sometimes a lifetime, gradually fading. That's why we still often see women on the street with blue eyebrows and eyes outlined with winged liner. Tattoos like that are no longer done today. Now the technique is called micropigmentation: it is performed with modern equipment and hypoallergenic water-based pigments with mineral ingredients, and the pigment goes no deeper than 1 mm into the skin. As a result, the effect looks natural, lasts no more than 2 years and fades gradually without leaving a trace. You can read more details here.

migx_questions.questions-title: Can micropigmentation be done during pregnancy or breastfeeding?
migx_questions.questions-text:
Pregnancy and breastfeeding are relative contraindications to micropigmentation. However, if the procedure is done without anesthesia (which is not allowed for women in this situation) and your health permits, semi-permanent makeup can be done.
It's important to note that not every area and technique can be done without anesthesia. In fact, only one technique is possible – powder brows, since it is a specific procedure in which the pigment is sprayed into the skin, so the pain is minimal. For lip and eyelid micropigmentation, however, anesthesia is mandatory, because the skin in these areas is thinner and has more capillaries, which makes the procedure more painful. Since a woman's perception and emotional state change during pregnancy, micropigmentation can become very uncomfortable.
If you decide on semi-permanent makeup, we recommend having it done in the third trimester or six months after giving birth, after consulting your doctor first.

Several factors determine how painful it is:

  • the area being treated – brows are less painful than the eyelids and lips;
  • who performs it – professional artists at micropigmentation studios work according to their qualifications and control how deep the pigment goes. This keeps pain to a minimum;
  • your individual pain threshold and emotional state during the micropigmentation procedure.

All techniques are performed with an anesthetic. It is applied not beforehand but during the procedure. This reduces pain, redness and swelling.

migx_questions.questions-title: Can a failed or old tattoo be covered with semi-permanent makeup?
migx_questions.questions-text: If an old tattoo was done a long time ago, the pigment was injected deep and the design has already changed color, it won't be possible to cover it. Fresh or unsuccessful semi-permanent makeup can be covered only if a new shape can be laid over it (for example, brows, eyeliner, or a larger, brighter shape). In all other cases, it's a waste of time and money. An old tattoo can stay in the skin for life, while micropigmentation lasts for a few years. So the new makeup will fade over time and reveal the old tattoo underneath. It's much simpler and safer to remove the tattoo with a laser and then, once the skin has regenerated, apply semi-permanent makeup. That way you'll get a gorgeous result – exactly the way it's supposed to look.
